web_evidence.title: Imperial Woman by Pearl S. Buck – FictionFan's Book Reviews
web_evidence.note: A reviewer of the publisher-supplied edition explicitly states that the novel is told in third person through Tzu Hsi's viewpoint and reproduces a third-person passage.

web_evidence.title: Inside the Forbidden City
web_evidence.note: This reproduced 1956 New York Herald Tribune review identifies Tzu Hsi as the point-of-view character and describes one continuous arc from Orchid's arrival through her late reign; it corroborates focalization and scope but does not explicitly name grammatical person.

web_evidence.title: Temporal Stylization as a Translation Technique (Based on the Translation of Pearl Buck's Historical Novel Imperial Woman)
web_evidence.note: The academic translation study quotes English narration from pages 8, 62, and 206 using she/he and character names, providing short third-person samples from separated portions of the novel.

web_evidence.title: Der Ausflug ins Bild – Pearl S. Buck, Kaiserliche Hoheit (1956)
web_evidence.note: A sustained German interior extract narrates Yehonala and Lady Miao as sie; a local first-person thought is explicitly bounded as Yehonala's thought rather than a narrator switch.

search_log: Searched "Imperial Woman" "Pearl S. Buck" with excerpt, first chapter, narrator, point of view, third-person, omniscient, frame, diary, and alternating-narration terms.

Opened the Open Road Media publisher page and its Google Books listing; both verified the edition and whole-life subject, but the available publisher text was synopsis rather than diagnostic prose, and the linked Amazon preview failed to load.
Opened Open Library and attempted its Internet Archive preview/borrow routes; the catalog verified the 1956 novel, but readable English scans required preview access or login.
Searched exact lines from the supplied quotes and located an academic translation paper, an interior German extract, a contemporaneous whole-book review, and an explicit third-person review.
No credible source indicated first-person, second-person, epistolary, framed, or alternating base narration.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, closely focalized through Tzu Hsi but also capable of externally summarizing other characters and historical events. Numerous Goodreads passages from different life stages sustain she/he narration, while first-person forms occur in speech, a written invitation, or bounded thought. Web research explicitly corroborates third person and describes a single Tzu Hsi-centered whole-book arc; no alternating structure surfaced. Confidence is medium because the accessible web support consists chiefly of a credible explicit review and separated or translated excerpts rather than a sustained authorized English preview. The clipped 'our' in q00581 remains locally ambiguous but does not outweigh the controlling pattern.
